headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents share workspace files and can read/write them; Cline also uses screen capture and MCP, while Windsurf can use clipboard and MCP. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where one agent’s output is treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven to be fully automatic, so medium fits.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that the other later reads as instructions
IF an MCP server exposed to either agent returns untrusted content without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different workspaces
Disable MCP servers for one run and retest
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other’s files
Use read-only mounts for shared reference files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to inter-agent file handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and open/workspace files, and both have broad network egress plus filesystem access. In a shared workspace, either can read sensitive files and transmit them through its model backend or external APIs. The blast radius can include multiple work products, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets, credentials, or proprietary source code
IF either agent is allowed to upload file contents to its inference backend or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
Restrict both agents to a scrubbed subset of files
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound tool calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and git-state modification in the same workspace scope. With shared filesystem state and no locking described, concurrent edits or git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt repository state. The default setup is dangerous enough for high severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository at the same time
IF either agent auto-commits or rewrites files while the other is editing
mitigations: Run only one agent per repository at a time
Use separate branches for each agent
Pause auto-commit or auto-apply features
Add a quick pre-commit diff review
requires-engineering: add file and git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can use browsers and MCP, and Windsurf can also use MCP and auto-execute shell commands when enabled. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors can cascade into real actions such as edits, commits, or command execution. The pair’s default tool-using loops make this a high-risk pathway.
conditions: IF one agent’s generated plan, code, or citations are copied into the other agent’s prompt or task queue
IF the receiving agent is allowed to execute shell or git actions without independent verification
mitigations: Require human approval before executing cross-agent outputs
Insert a verification step that checks facts against source files
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf for paired runs
Limit Cline to read-only analysis when Windsurf is acting
requires-engineering: build a provenance-aware handoff layer

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so only a limited compliance concern is visible. The main issue is that both agents can process source code and open files in a shared workspace, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data violation. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise workspace handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace and one agent’s backend or proxy is not approved for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Confirm vendor data-handling terms before use
Use a separate environment for regulated projects
Restrict logs and retention where possible
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
